trust_decision.summary: No in-code trust decision: the advisory is CWE-1395 (dependency on a vulnerable/unmaintained component). All E2EE crypto (Olm/Megolm sessions, ed25519 signature verification, SAS) is delegated to python-olm/libolm, and the fix swaps that whole backend for vodozemac.

landing_point.why: The summary names the olm dependency, so an engineer would go to the python-olm pin first and then to the wrapper classes in src/nio/crypto/sessions.py.

fix_sites.entry_point: nio.crypto.OlmAccount / Session / InboundSession / OutboundSession / InboundGroupSession / OutboundGroupSession (public classes exported from nio.crypto)
Olm.verify_json, reached from AsyncClient.keys_query / sync device-key handling

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable: there is no check to bypass. The fix is a full crypto-backend port, and the 'protection' is just no longer depending on libolm.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing libolm-format pickles in the sqlite store have to keep loading (the fix adds a libolm-pickle fallback and an upgrade on save). Separately, the legacy 'hmac-sha256' SAS MAC method was dropped, which breaks verification with peers that only offer the old MAC.

O6_input_shapes: olm message type 0 (pre-key) vs type 1 (normal) ciphertext
vodozemac-format vs libolm-format (v<4 and v4) pickles
SAS MAC method hkdf-hmac-sha256 vs legacy hmac-sha256
O9_family: CWE-1395 dependency on vulnerable third-party component (libolm crypto backend replacement)

O10_build.toolchain: pip / pyproject (setuptools); the e2e extra needs python-olm (native libolm C library) at the pinned commit, or vodozemac (Rust wheel) after the fix

j.j_sites_touched: pyproject.toml, src/nio/crypto/__init__.py, src/nio/crypto/olm_machine.py, src/nio/crypto/sas.py, src/nio/crypto/sessions.py, src/nio/store/__init__.py, src/nio/store/database.py
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bump or re-pin python-olm, or wrap libolm calls, instead of porting every crypto primitive to vodozemac while keeping old pickles loadable.

out_of_scope_notes: The legacy SAS MAC 'hmac-sha256' (calculate_mac_long_kdf) is still negotiable at the pinned commit (src/nio/crypto/sas.py:471-474). The fix removes it as part of the port, but it is protocol hygiene, not the advisory's own check.
unverified: The advisory text itself was not available; the CVE-2022-39255 / CVE-2024-45193 mechanisms (libolm issues) were not checked against code, because they live in libolm, not in this repo.
repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo flag not assessed.
O1 set to 0 because there is no single flaw with entry points; every E2EE public API reaches the replaced backend.
Whether the e2e test suite runs offline after install was not verified by running it; inferred from the tests using a local sqlite store and data files.
